q: What is tolerance?
a: Permissible deviation from a plan for a delegated level of management.

q: Who authorizes an exception plan?
a: The project board authorizes a replacement stage or project plan within its authority.

q: What is the daily log?
a: Part of the project log for informal issues, notes and observations.

q: What are the seven performance targets?
a: Benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, risk and sustainability.

q: The graphic engine is forecast to finish three weeks late against a one week stage time tolerance. What should Zosia do?
a: Send an exception report to the project board. A forecast beyond stage tolerance requires escalation.

q: Artur receives an exception report. What may the project board decide?
a: Request an exception plan, change tolerances within its authority, or close the project. The board makes the management level decision.

q: What report does Zosia send Artur regularly about stage progress?
a: Highlight report. The project manager sends highlight reports to the project board.

q: A work package is forecast two days late within a three day tolerance. What should the team manager do?
a: Manage within tolerance and report progress to the project manager. A delay within tolerance does not automatically require an exception.

q: Where does Zosia keep day to day informal notes before formal entries are required?
a: Daily log in the project log. The project log includes a daily log.

q: Why does managing by exception save project board time?
a: The board receives regular summaries and intervenes when tolerance is forecast to be exceeded. Authority is delegated within agreed tolerances.

q: What does a forecast mean in progress control?
a: An estimate of the future state using current information. Forecasts support decisions before an exception occurs.

q: Does a two day delay always constitute an exception?
a: No; compare the forecast with the relevant tolerance. A deviation alone does not establish an exception.

q: Who receives a checkpoint report from the team manager?
a: Project manager. Checkpoint reports communicate team progress to the project manager.

q: Who receives a highlight report from the project manager?
a: Project board. Highlight reports provide periodic board level status.

q: When should Zosia send an exception report?
a: When the stage forecast exceeds its tolerance. The project manager escalates a forecast stage exception.

q: Which report summarizes the whole project at closure?
a: End project report. It compares overall performance against the project baseline.

q: How many project performance targets does PRINCE2 7 include?
a: Seven, including sustainability. Sustainability joins time, cost, quality, scope, benefits and risk.

q: What does Tomek do when a work package is forecast outside its tolerance?
a: Escalate to the project manager. The team manager cannot unilaterally change delegated tolerance.

q: How many performance targets are used to control a PRINCE2 7 project?
a: Seven. The seven targets include sustainability.

q: A report from the project manager about a forecast tolerance breach is an exception [...].
a: Report. The exception report supports an authorized decision.
